role: Machine Learning Engineer, AWS Analytics Engineering
responsibilities: Own and evolve system architecture. Design and implement scalable, secure, and cost effective distributed systems for workflow orchestration and AI powered analytics. Make sound technical trade offs between short term delivery and long term maintainability.
Drive architectural decisions that impact petabyte scale data processing and thousands of jobs.
Build multi agent AI systems. Design, implement, and optimize multi agent architectures including autonomous agents, orchestration frameworks, and tool integrations
Build reusable components, APIs, and micro-services that other teams adopt. Continuously simplify, optimize, and remove bottlenecks across the stack.

Drive platform capabilities end to end. Own features from concept through deployment and operation. Examples include building new marketplace and IDE experiences, implementing validated query patterns, designing cross service governed metrics, or creating real time monitoring dashboards.
Solve complex ambiguous problems. Navigate unclear requirements and competing priorities to deliver innovative solutions.
Influence technical direction and mentor others. Provide technical leadership across the team and adjacent teams.
Drive operational excellence. Own the operational health of production systems.
Innovate with AI/ML technologies. Stay current with GenAI, LLM, and ML advancements.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: ensuring our systems are reliable, secure, and performant at scale
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: rigour: the role balances new capabilities against "operational excellence, ensuring our systems are reliable, secure, and performant at scale", with no velocity phrases beyond one mention of short term delivery.
evidence.domain_risk: directly influence how AWS leadership makes decisions
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: moderate: errors would mislead internal decisions ("directly influence how AWS leadership makes decisions") but the posting names no financial reporting or regulatory exposure.
evidence.collaboration_width: data engineers; applied scientists; product managers; business analysts
evidence.data_team_maturity: The AWS Analytics Engineering (AAE) organization is the analytics backbone of AWS
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: mature: an established organisation that is "the analytics backbone of AWS" and processes data "at petabyte scale".
evidence.jd_authorship: implementing validated query patterns, designing cross service governed metrics
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: mixed: specific bullets on multi agent architectures and "validated query patterns" sit beside amazon boilerplate such as "Solve complex ambiguous problems".
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: internal_data: the role builds the data platform and platform services that "serve hundreds of internal customers".
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: strategic: the role is told to "Own and evolve system architecture" and "Drive architectural decisions".
evidence.ai_role_explanation: ai_enabler: the candidate builds the AI systems themselves ("Build multi agent AI systems", "GenAI powered analytics capabilities").
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: tool_listed: testing appears only as software life cycle experience in the preferred qualifications, with no data quality ownership.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Own the operational health of production systems
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: moderate: the fear is production outages ("Own the operational health of production systems"), not compliance or bad data reaching leadership.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: balance building new capabilities with operational excellence
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: mixed: building new multi agent systems and marketplace experiences sits beside "Continuously simplify, optimize, and remove bottlenecks".
evidence.loss_aversion: Drive operational excellence. Own the operational health of production systems. The fear is production downtime on a platform used across AWS.
